historical_reviews.deepseek: Maps Hdd to a generic disk token but cannot prove which disk or bootloader is selected, exposes credentials and lacks readback, boot evidence and cleanup.
historical_reviews.gpt_v2: Correctly requires a stable disk-to-boot-entry identity and positive POST/OS evidence rather than treating command success as boot success.
historical_reviews.history: No earlier exact source identity record exists.
historical_reviews.v3_1: HDD is a device class, not a unique target. On a multi-disk UEFI system, acceptance must bind physical serial or WWN to the Boot#### entry and then to the expected OS root/filesystem identity.

original_test_intent: Validate that the BMC's enabled one-time HDD setting boots the approved SUT from the intended local disk and bootloader, then leaves normal boot configuration and storage unchanged.
original_method: Map exact disk serial or WWN to controller path, UEFI Boot#### or legacy entry, bootloader and expected OS/root identity; capture baseline state, obtain approval, apply and read back the protected one-time HDD override, reboot once under POST/console observation, prove that mapped disk and OS were reached without writes beyond normal boot, then verify override consumption and restore the original boot baseline.
manual_activity: The owner selects the exact disk/boot entry and approves the reboot; an operator observes POST/console, prevents installer or recovery writes and controls restoration, recovery and verdict.
required_inputs: UEFI Boot#### or legacy disk mapping
Expected bootloader, OS and root/filesystem marker
Baseline boot order and current override
safety_requirements: Do not treat generic disk as a unique target
Use one-time scope and protected credentials
Read back the setting before reboot
Stop on wrong disk, recovery/installer, write prompt, boot failure or timeout
Never perform repair or installation as part of this boot check
Preserve logs and do not automatically retry
agent_execution_scope: Collect boot, disk and health baseline
Validate exact disk and boot-entry mapping
Apply/read back one approved one-time HDD setting after confirmation
Request and perform one approved reboot
Collect structured state while operator proves POST/console and OS/root identity
Verify override consumption and restored health
engineer_actions: Observe selected disk and safe OS boot

command_applicability.original_deepseek_command_fit: bootdev disk expresses only a broad class; the literal command exposes credentials, resets immediately and cannot prove the physical disk, UEFI entry, bootloader, OS root or one-time cleanup.
command_applicability.command_recommendation: Use the vendor-supported protected one-time HDD control after mapping it to the owner-selected disk; correlate readback, POST and OS root identity, then prove override consumption and restoration.
command_applicability.original_parameters_and_time_preserved: Hdd, Enabled/Save, reboot and 10/20-minute estimates remain; specific path becomes the approved disk/bootloader/OS mapping.

modernized_recommendation.recommended_method: Maintain an identity chain from disk serial/WWN and controller slot to firmware boot entry, bootloader evidence and mounted root UUID, bounded by pre/post boot-control state.
modernized_recommendation.difference_from_original_method: Makes a generic HDD selection objectively attributable to one local disk while retaining the same reboot test.
modernized_recommendation.coverage_difference: Returning to an OS does not prove the intended disk was selected when mirrored, duplicate or fallback boot entries exist.
modernized_recommendation.risks_limitations: Firmware may choose the first enumerated disk or a fallback Boot#### entry; device numbering can change across boots, so stable serial/WWN and filesystem identifiers are required.

project_override_considerations: The Project must name the intended disk and OS marker and disposition the copied PXE regression note as non-HDD context unless separate HDD-specific regression behavior is approved.
expected_evidence: Approved target/window, disk serial/WWN/controller, boot entry/bootloader/OS-root mapping and baseline order
Disk health/backup and protected one-time HDD write/readback
Reset plus POST/console timeline proving the mapped disk and bootloader
OS/root/filesystem identity and health with no installer/recovery write
Consumed/cleared override and restored original boot configuration
Audit/SEL/OS logs, recovery actions and engineer-owned verdict

source_conflict_analysis.analysis: Items and procedure consistently require HDD boot. The specific path is the project-selected disk/boot entry, while the PXE regression note is copied context and does not impose a competing HDD target.

blocked_analysis.analysis: The exact disk mapping, boot marker and recovery package are normal owner/vendor inputs; the engineering workflow remains identifiable without guessing them.

review_improvement: Replaces generic disk-token success with a stable physical-disk, boot-entry and OS identity chain plus safe one-time cleanup.
independent_technical_reasoning: Disk enumeration labels are not stable identities, and UEFI firmware may select a boot entry whose loader resides on a different disk than the eventual root filesystem. Correlating WWN, Boot#### device path, loader and root UUID is necessary to demonstrate that the intended local storage path—not a fallback—satisfied the case.
